ana: Quick heads-up: starting bring-up for cormorant-4b (community checkpoint). License includes 'no commercial redistribution' and a line about 'derivative binary artifacts' + attribution. Can we surface a quantized 4-bit variant behind Hosted/Dedicated without giving customers raw files?

jiro: Paste the exact snippet? small wording changes matter a lot.

ana: Copied from LICENSE: ```
Redistribution: The model weights and any derivative binary artifacts (including quantized weight files or compiled kernels) may not be redistributed for commercial purposes. Hosting the model to provide API inference is permitted provided the binaries are not publicly distributed. Attribution: Products using the model must credit the Original Authors and link to the LICENSE.
```

mari: From ML experiments: did a 4-bit GPTQ pass on dev. Latency 2.2x, MMLU down 1.3 pts, summary Rouge-L -1.0, safety classifier FPR +0.4. Embedding sim to fp16 ~0.975. Looks workable but want full eval before canary.

ops-bot: Ingest scan: cormorant-4b fp16 upload at s3://models/internal/cormorant-4b/2026-03-25/; no quant artifacts found. Metadata tag license=CMR-1. Public ACL=false.

jiro: Legal angle: looks serve-only friendly but "derivative binary artifacts" explicitly covers quant files. Need a written counsel note that API serving is OK if we never distribute binaries. Also watch customer-hosted Dedicated — handing them files may be considered redistribution.

legal: Counsel note (short): "Serving outputs via API is permitted under CMR-1 provided weight binaries and derivative artifacts are not redistributed. For Dedicated customer-hosted deployments where customers receive binaries, obtain a signed exception forbidding downstream redistribution or deny binary access. Attribution as proposed is acceptable. Recording memo in compliance tracker."

mari: Good. While legal memo is in tracker I can run full eval suite and add prompt-level diffs. If legal signs off, plan: 1) gate quantized variant to Hosted + Dedicated serve-only (deny-download), 2) force provenance header + UI attribution, 3) provide fp16 fallback route for safety-sensitive endpoints.

ops-bot: Proposed infra controls: a) deny_export hook when metadata.license=="CMR-1"; b) scrub any public/temporary buckets for quant artifacts; c) restrict download roles to [security, compliance]; d) ensure backups encrypted and not accessible to customer-controlled VMs. Opening PR now.

ana: Also need to consider KMS/HSM custody for Dedicated/private customers—if a customer insists on self-hosting, the license likely disallows giving them binaries. We should add a compliance checklist entry so sales/solutions know the exception path involves negotiating a different license.

jeval-bot: Quick eval summary uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/cormorant-4b/quant-eval-2026-03-25.csv \u2014 MMLU: base 60.8 -> 59.5, HellaSwag 85.2 -> 84.3, Rouge-L -1.0; Safety FPR +0.4; Embedding sim 0.975. Full diffs in artifact.

jiro: Action items: Mari run per-prompt regression to see safety hotspots; Ops implement deny_export+scrub PR; Legal file memo (done) and add exception guidance; Ana draft attribution copy + provenance header format. We'll keep canary internal until eval + infra controls in place.

mari: Starting prompt-level runs now and will post findings in the eval doc. If quality looks stable we can move to internal canary with the controls above.

ana: Draft attribution text: "Cormorant-4B  Cormorant Research Collective. Licensed under CMR-1. See LICENSE." Proposed provenance header: `X-Model-Provenance: cormorant-4b;license=CMR-1;quantized=4bit;artifact_date=2026-03-25`

ops-bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/infra/artifacts/+/712 \u2014 implements deny_export when license=CMR-1, schedules scrub jobs for any public quant artifacts, restricts download links, and adds audit logging.

legal: Uploaded memo to compliance tracker with guidance for customer-hosted exceptions.

ana: Thanks all — leaving thread open until internal canary RFC is merged and infra PR is in. :white_check_mark:
